Google BigQuery

Source: vignettes/bigquery.Rmd
bigquery.Rmd

BigQuery is Google’s hosted analytics database. You submit SQL query jobs without managing a database server. Run GoogleSQL in a Shiny app using each visitor’s Google account. bigquery$query() returns a data frame you can display with renderTable().

The first app checks which Google account is signed in. You can then use the same client to query your tables.

Try the guided demo

Run shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("bigquery") in your R console. The guide asks for the query project ID and OAuth client_id, explains the consent screen and test users, then asks for the Web client’s secret through masked input. Install processx, jsonlite and askpass first. No database driver is needed. You can save a draft while arranging access.

The editable app runs SELECT SESSION_USER() only after you click Run example query. Its default location = "US" suits the identity query; set it to your dataset’s location before querying tables. The default maximum_bytes_billed = "10000000" limits bytes a query may bill. For scripts, supply project, client_id and optionally those settings, set OAUTHDB_BIGQUERY_CLIENT_SECRET, and use prompt = FALSE. See Guided cloud demos for editing and resuming.

With no account yet, BigQuery sandbox offers a starting point without a billing account. You still need to enable the API, configure your Web OAuth client and have permission to run jobs. The full OAuth demo has not been verified against a sandbox account.

Google Cloud setup

Create a Web OAuth client in Google Cloud and configure its consent screen. Register http://localhost:8100 as the redirect URI and enable the BigQuery API for the query project.

Users need permission to run query jobs in that project and read the data. BigQuery bills queries to this project. Set location to match your datasets; this example uses "EU".

Save the client ID and secret in a local .Renviron file and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

In Google Cloud Console, select the app project and open Google Auth Platform. Configure Branding and Audience; if the app is in testing, add the Google accounts that will try it. Under Clients, create a Web application and add http://localhost:8100 to authorized redirect URIs. Copy its client ID and secret. Google’s web-app OAuth guide explains consent and deployment requirements.

Setting Where to find it
project Cloud Console project selector: copy the project ID, not its display name or number
location BigQuery Explorer: open the dataset’s details and copy its location
Client ID and secret Google Auth Platform Clients, the Web application

Ask the administrator for BigQuery Job User on the query project and BigQuery Data Viewer on the relevant datasets, or equivalent narrower permissions. See BigQuery IAM roles. The initial identity query still creates a job and needs a query project.

A complete app

Save this as example.R, replacing "billing-project" with your project ID:

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_bigquery_client(
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  bigquery <- oauth_db_bigquery_api(
    auth$connection,
    project = "billing-project",
    location = "EU"
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    bigquery$query("SELECT SESSION_USER() AS signed_in_user")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)

Run source("example.R") and open http://localhost:8100. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the output.

Query your data

Replace the identity query with SQL for your tables. Use project.dataset.table names when the data is in another project.

For values entered by a user, pass named R values in parameters. This example assumes a reporting.Orders table with a country column:

output$rows <- renderTable({
  bigquery$query(
    "SELECT * FROM reporting.Orders WHERE country = @country LIMIT 20",
    parameters = list(country = "NL")
  )
})

Find datasets and tables

$datasets() lists dataset IDs in the project; $tables("reporting") lists the table IDs in that dataset. Add these outputs inside server():

output$datasets <- renderPrint(bigquery$datasets())
output$tables <- renderPrint(bigquery$tables("reporting"))

Add verbatimTextOutput("datasets") and verbatimTextOutput("tables") to the UI. To use reporting as the default dataset in SQL, set dataset = "reporting" when creating the BigQuery client.

Query costs and larger results

Set maximum_bytes_billed = "1000000000" on $query() to limit the bytes a query may bill. LIMIT restricts the rows returned, but doesn’t provide the same cost limit.

Queries run synchronously and collect all result pages into R memory. Choose queries whose results fit in memory. A timeout or sign-out stops fetching results; it doesn’t cancel a submitted BigQuery job.

Result types

INT64 and decimal columns remain strings to preserve precision. Dates become Date, timestamps become UTC POSIXct, and nested or repeated fields use list columns.

Use raw = TRUE to inspect the REST result and schema. ?oauth_db_bigquery_api describes parameter types and other options. For saved results or background work, see Authentication and sessions.
